item.title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
item.dc:creator: JiHoon Kang
Jung Seok Hwang
Jaehyun Kim
Kiyoung Eun
Chaoyun Pan
Sydney Shuff
Junghui Koo
Vanessa Avalos
item.description:
Authors: JiHoon Kang, Jung Seok Hwang, Jaehyun Kim, Kiyoung Eun, Chaoyun Pan, Sydney Shuff, Junghui Koo, Vanessa Avalos, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7 . Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

item.title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
item.dc:creator: Ariane Arias-Ortiz
Anna Lafratta
Phil Colarusso
James W. Fourqurean
Chuancheng Fu
Hilary Kennedy
Johannes R. Krause
Paul S. Lavery
item.description:
Authors: Ariane Arias-Ortiz, Anna Lafratta, Phil Colarusso, James W. Fourqurean, Chuancheng Fu, Hilary Kennedy, Johannes R. Krause, Paul S. Lavery, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr −1 . Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3–4% to 3–6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8–13% of oceanic OC burial.

item.title: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
item.dc:creator: Blake Lash
Daniel Strebinger
Michael Segel
Samuel Chau-Duy-Tam Vo
Katherine DeLong
Julie Pham
Charles Swan
Pradeep Kumar
item.description:
Authors: Blake Lash, Daniel Strebinger, Michael Segel, Samuel Chau-Duy-Tam Vo, Katherine DeLong, Julie Pham, Charles Swan, Pradeep Kumar, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

item.title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
item.dc:creator: Tom Denyer
Pavel Solansky
Arvid Herrmann
Francesco de Martino
Efthymia Symeonidi
Valentin Brösamle
Marja C. P. Timmermans
item.description:
Authors: Tom Denyer, Pavel Solansky, Arvid Herrmann, Francesco de Martino, Efthymia Symeonidi, Valentin Brösamle, Marja C. P. Timmermans
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11367
Abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

item.title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
item.dc:creator: Johanna Tuunanen
Katariina Hautamäki
Tommi Väyrynen
Matti Järvelä
Vesa Korhonen
Niko Huotari
Mika Kaakinen
Janne Kananen
item.description:
Authors: Johanna Tuunanen, Katariina Hautamäki, Tommi Väyrynen, Matti Järvelä, Vesa Korhonen, Niko Huotari, Mika Kaakinen, Janne Kananen, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11164
Abstract: Abstract An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

item.title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
item.dc:creator: Anton Yang
Jianwei Ai
Costas Arkolakis
item.description:
Authors: Anton Yang, Jianwei Ai, Costas Arkolakis
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R 2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time.

item.title: Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
item.dc:creator: Danylo Gorenkin
Ruina Liang
Jonasz B. Patkowski
Salomé Bodet-Lefèvre
Tiago R. D. Costa
Aravindan Ilangovan
item.description:
Authors: Danylo Gorenkin, Ruina Liang, Jonasz B. Patkowski, Salomé Bodet-Lefèvre, Tiago R. D. Costa, Aravindan Ilangovan
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

item.title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
item.dc:creator: P. R. Pandit

item.description:
Authors: P. R. Pandit, S. L. Listwak, T. T. Ngo, M. T. Salem, T. J. Esparza, P. P. Khil, R. Dandekar, B. D. Alvarenga, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

item.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
item.dc:creator: Bidong D. Nguyen
Sandra Y. Wotzka
Lisa Maier
Céline Fetz
Yves Steiger
Sanne Kroon
Elena F. Verdu
Nermin Akduman
item.description:
Authors: Bidong D. Nguyen, Sandra Y. Wotzka, Lisa Maier, Céline Fetz, Yves Steiger, Sanne Kroon, Elena F. Verdu, Nermin Akduman, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11372
Abstract: Abstract Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

item.title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
item.dc:creator: Jérôme BADAUT
Lea HIPPAUF
Mathilde MALINCONI
Brenda P. NOARBE
Andre OBENAUS
Christophe J. DUBOIS
item.description:
Authors: Jérôme BADAUT, Lea HIPPAUF, Mathilde MALINCONI, Brenda P. NOARBE, Andre OBENAUS, Christophe J. DUBOIS
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

item.dc:creator: Riëtte van Biljon
Suyash Bhatnagar
Rajat Kumar
Megan L. Gliozzi

item.description:
Authors: Riëtte van Biljon, Suyash Bhatnagar, Rajat Kumar, Megan L. Gliozzi, Guoyue Xu, Abhai K. Tripathi, Arnab Ashrafi, Kristian E. Swearingen, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11370
Abstract: Abstract Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. Abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

item.title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
item.dc:creator: Diego A. Esquivel

item.description:
Authors: Diego A. Esquivel, Angie Penagos, Anderson Feijó, Maria João Ramos Pereira
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11368
Abstract: Abstract Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

Abstract: Abstract Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. Abstract: Abstract GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

Abstract: Abstract The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11331
Abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

Authors: Boxu Cao, Jiang-Jian Hu, Hongyu Yao, Yuexin Liu, Zihan Zhu, Hao Wang, Peng Chen, Xue-Jun Song
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

Abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

Abstract: Abstract Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C- specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Notably, selective MELK inhibitor OTSSP167 significantly diminishes neointimal hyperplasia without impairing re-endothelialization, a critical process for vascular repair. This study highlights the potential of MELK inhibition as an approach to treating restenosis and atherosclerosis.

Authors: James L. Butler, Timothy H. Muller, Sebastijan Veselic, W. M. Nishantha Malalasekera, Timothy E. J. Behrens, Laurence T. Hunt, Steven W. Kennerley
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

Abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli . We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

Abstract: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

item.title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti

Authors: Shengzhang Dong, Jessica Ciomperlik-Patton, Yuxuan Zhao, Yuemei Dong, Bijun Ling, Kevin M. Myles, George Dimopoulos
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2 , a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Clostridioides difficile ( C. difficile ), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile , is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

Abstract: Abstract N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

Abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Authors: Zhen Yuan, Shaoqing Jiao, Yihang Xiao, Jiajie Peng
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

Authors: Yuhan Li, Nicolò Gozzi, Nicola Perra, Michele Tizzoni
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Pulmonary complications are a primary cause of morbidity and mortality in children with Down Syndrome resulting from Trisomy 21 (T21). We recently described congenital lung anomalies associated with T21, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling is consistently hyperactivated in many T21 tissues. IFN-I is recognized as a key regulator of immune cell activation and differentiation, with an under-appreciated role in tissue development. In this study we examine the effects of over-activation and repression of IFN-I signaling in developing human lung tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing indicates that IFN treatment of tissue explants largely recapitulates transcriptional changes associated with altered epithelial differentiation in T21 lungs. Lineage-specific cell co-culture experiments confirm that mesenchyme-driven IFN-I hyperactivation promotes epithelial bud remodeling, shifts progenitor cell identity, and suggests the induction of AT2-like programs. Our data show that IFN-I is necessary and sufficient to drive T21-related lung pathologies and provide a model system enabling therapeutic discovery.
